change_summary: Ran a runtime-only deterministic two-stage meta-allocation experiment across the same late / mid / old fixed OHLCV snapshots. The strict weak-tape detector was held fixed, and only the stage-two action changed: on `stress_strict` days, `trend_long` signals alone were de-risked to `0.5x` or `0.25x`. Entries, exits, ranking, breakout sizing, and accepted A+B cohort rules all stayed unchanged. No repository trading logic was kept after measurement.
component: runtime-only monkeypatch of `portfolio_engine.size_signals()` with a day-pointer hook for fixed-snapshot replay, applying trend-only haircuts on cached strict-stress dates (rolled back; no repo trading logic changed)

delta_metrics.note: This removes the last obvious sleeve-target ambiguity for the current strict weak-tape detector. The result is again vacuous by construction: the detector never intersected an actual trend sizing event in any replay window, so changing the action strength could not matter.

hypothesis: If the strict weak-tape detector from exp-20260423-014 has zero useful overlap with `breakout_long`, perhaps the correct sleeve target is `trend_long`: keep `stress_strict = breadth_above_200 <= 0.55 AND spy_pct_from_ma <= -0.02` fixed, but de-risk trend signals only on those days. A valid result should show non-zero candidate overlap and improve at least one weaker window without harming the strong window.
